summary: Dedicated pool throughput drop during quiet windows; transient GPU thinness traced to sidecar burst spike
description:
Issue summary:
- Customer (QuillSync) reports periodic dedicated-pool throughput drop during their midday quiet windows (low traffic), recurring over 3 days. Affected routes are pinned to dedicated pool in us-west-2.
Impact:
- P50/P95 throughput decreased by ~30% for 2-6 minute windows; increased request queueing and observed fallback to shared tier for a subset of requests. Customer-facing latency spikes and elevated 429/504 retries.
Environment:
- prod:us-west-2, dedicated pool: quillsync-prod-pool-1, models: redwood/open-13b and redwood/opt-6.7b, customer_tier: dedicated.
Steps to reproduce:
1) Traffic profile: send steady low-rate traffic mimicking QuillSync background sync (10-15 concurrent short streams).
2) Wait for scheduled telemetry window (~midday, customer local timezone).
3) Observe allocator/gpu attach logs and autoscaler events for pool quillsync-prod-pool-1.
Observed behavior:
- Short windows of GPU availability thinness (slots reduce), autoscaler does not immediately scale up, queueing increases, routing starts falling back or throttling routes.
- Sidecar metrics show large short-lived burst of connections/metrics flushes coincident with drop windows.
Expected behavior:
- Dedicated pool should maintain steady attach capacity for pinned routes through quiet windows; autoscaler should respond within configured cooldowns to legitimate load shifts.
Initial pointers and logs:
- Customer-provided request traces: trace IDs attached in comments.
- SRE dashboard snapshot: p50 throughput chart and allocator-attach-count for quillsync-prod-pool-1 during 2026-03-11 to 2026-03-13.
- Sidecar metrics: telemetry-flush-rate spiked for multiple tenants at the same timestamps.
comments: 2026-03-13 10:12 - Maya Singh: Customer opened with sample traces and heap of request IDs. They see mid-day short windows (2-6m) where throughput drops and retries spike. Provided correlation with their background job times.
2026-03-13 11:05 - Support (Ethan Park): Acknowledged. Asked for pool name, model pins, and asked SRE to pull allocator logs and sidecar flush metrics for us-west-2. First-response SLA noted.

2026-03-13 13:40 - SRE (Lina Gomez): Pulled allocator and attach logs. Noted rapid ephemeral increase in sidecar emit events (metrics flush) at the same timestamps. Allocator reported short attach failures and temporary slot release. Sharing logs: /logs/quill/attach-2026-03-11-13.tar.gz (internal).

2026-03-13 15:20 - Support (Ethan Park): Asked customer to temporarily stagger their background syncs as a mitigation while we continue investigation. Customer tried and reported partial mitigation but not full elimination.

2026-03-14 09:02 - SRE (Lina Gomez): Observed that the autoscaler backoff combined with ephemeral sidecar CPU spikes caused attach latency to exceed autoscale thresholds, preventing timely scale-up. Hypothesis added to investigation notes.

2026-03-14 12:45 - Engineering (Raj Patel): Looking at sidecar commit history; flagged recent telemetry-batching change two weeks ago that increased synchronous flushes on low-traffic tenants. Opening PR to decouple flush scheduling from request thread. Refer PR in related_github_prs.

2026-03-14 14:30 - Ethan Park: Notified customer of ongoing engineering work and provided recommended temporary config: set autoscaler.cooldown_ms to 30000 and sidecar.metrics_batch_max to 100 for their pool as a mitigation. Customer accepted temporary change for testing.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Sidecar synchronous metric/connection flush spikes briefly consume CPU on node sidecars, delaying allocator attach handshakes and causing temporary slot releases in dedicated pool.
Hypothesis 2: Autoscaler cooldown/backoff logic treats attach latency as noise and delays scaling decisions; combined with brief attach failures this allows a cascade to queueing and fallbacks.

Telemetry checked: allocator-attach-latency, slot-count, sidecar-cpu, sidecar-metrics-flush-rate, autoscaler-evaluation-latency. Correlated sidecar-flush spikes with attach-latency spikes at 13:02-13:06 UTC across 3 days.

Trace sampling: captured three request traces where attach returned transient 504 while GPU slot showed released then reattached within 20s. Traces: trace-20260311-13a, trace-20260312-13b, trace-20260313-13c (internal IDs).
Reproduce attempts: Internal load test injecting synthetic metrics flush bursts on a small dedicated pool reproduced attach lag and p50 throughput drop within 90s.
resolution_notes: Short-term mitigation applied (2026-03-14 14:35): temporarily adjusted autoscaler.cooldown_ms to 30000 for quillsync-prod-pool-1 and reduced sidecar.metrics_batch_max to 100 for the tenant’s sidecars. Customer reported immediate improvement in throughput valley duration reduced from 3-6m to <60s.

Root cause (provisional): recent telemetry batching change caused synchronous flush spikes on low-throughput tenants; these spikes increase sidecar CPU and block attach handshakes, which combined with conservative autoscaler thresholds produced temporary GPU thinness.

Permanent fix plan: engineering PR to decouple metric flushing from request-processing threads and add jittered flush windows for low-traffic tenants. Also update autoscaler to detect transient attach failures versus sustained load and avoid entering backoff for short-lived attach latency. PRs and rollout plan tracked in related_github_prs. Targeted rollout to staging then canary in us-west-2 over 2 weeks.

Follow-ups: 1) Post-deploy follow-up ticket to validate canary behavior and p99/p50 throughput during previous quiet windows. 2) Update Sidecar Runbook with recommended defaults for metrics batching for dedicated pools. 3) Offer customer a dedicated monitor dashboard and weekly check-in during rollout.
Status: Engineering work in progress; customer notified and mitigation remains in place.
